slots.label: once per repo
slots.title: Set up the repo
slots.text: Tell it where issues live, which triage labels you use and where docs go. Every other skill reads these answers, so you only do this once.

slots.label: align
slots.title: Coffee and a grilling
slots.text: Describe the change in one sentence. The agent asks one question at a time, each with a recommended answer. New terms go into the glossary, and hard decisions become ADRs. For non-code plans, use `/grill-me`.

slots.label: plan
slots.title: Spec, then tickets
slots.text: The whole conversation becomes a spec in your issue tracker. Then it gets cut into tracer-bullet tickets. Each ticket is a thin slice through every layer, and the blocking edges show which ones can start now.

slots.label: build
slots.title: Build ticket by ticket
slots.text: The agent works test-first at the seams you agreed on (`tdd`), then reviews its own diff against your coding standards and against the spec (`code-review`). You review the result, not every keystroke.

slots.label: uh-oh
slots.title: Something weird breaks
slots.text: Say “diagnose this”. Instead of guessing at fixes, the agent works through gates: reproduce, shrink the case, rank hypotheses, add instrumentation, fix, then lock it in with a regression test.

slots.label: ship
slots.title: Open the pull request
slots.text: The body has a summary, before/after evidence and an explicit merge-danger call, so your reviewer knows how carefully to look.

slots.label: reflect
slots.title: Retro, or hand off for tomorrow
slots.text: `/retro` suggests fixes to your environment, worst problem first: a slow test command, a missing glossary term, a vague CLAUDE.md rule. If the work isn't finished, `/handoff` compacts the session into a document a fresh agent can continue from.

slots.label: every few days
slots.title: Survey the codebase
slots.text: It scans for deepening opportunities, shows an HTML report, then grills you on the one you pick. Matt calls it “a survey, not a rescue.”
